Why no sign-up matters

Almost every "demo account" in crypto is a marketing funnel: register, confirm your email, sometimes pass KYC — and only then practice, inside an exchange app whose real goal is your first deposit. Binance's testnet needs an account and runs on an isolated test order book; Bybit's and OKX's demos need registration too.

MarginPad flips that: the simulator IS the product. It opens instantly, keeps your practice trades in your browser, and never pushes a deposit — because there is nothing to deposit. If you later want the social layer (paid 14-day season leaderboards, missions that earn real USDT, duels, profiles), a free account adds it. But that is your choice, not a gate.

Private by default

No sign-up also means nothing to leak: no email address in a database, no identity documents, no phone number. Practice trading is a learning activity — it should not require handing over personal data. If you do create an account later, it is a username and password, and the rewards system explains exactly what it needs and why.

Frequently asked questions

Is it really no sign-up?

Yes. The terminal opens and trades immediately — no email, no password, no KYC, no card, nothing to install. Your practice balance and trades are kept in your browser.

What do I miss without an account?

Only the social layer: 14-day season leaderboards with real USDT prizes, daily missions that pay, XP levels, duels and a public trader profile. The full trading simulator itself works without any account.

Does it use real prices?

Yes — live prices stream from a real exchange feed and fills happen at the current market price, with real leverage and liquidation mechanics.

Does it work on mobile?

Yes. The simulator runs in the browser on desktop and mobile, with a full-screen mobile chart mode. Nothing to download from an app store.

How long can I use it for free?

Forever. There is no trial clock, no locked features behind a card, and no deposit — the simulator is free, permanently.

How is this different from Binance testnet or exchange demos?

Exchange demo accounts require registration (and often KYC), and Binance testnet runs on an isolated order book with test prices. MarginPad needs no account at all and fills at live market prices.
